Pompeii History for Sleep 🌙 A Night with a Baker

Premieres Fri 30 Oct at 5 PM ET (21:00 UTC) · About 59 min · narrated slowly for sleep

Find it on our YouTube channel

The video goes public on the channel at the premiere time.

Life in ancient Pompeii, told for sleep: one calm night with a Roman baker, from the donkey mills to the first bread before dawn.

🌙 No mid-video ads, nothing to wake you.

In the bakery of Modestus, archaeologists found eighty-one round loaves still inside the oven, turned to charcoal but keeping their shape. Tonight's Pompeii history for sleep spends one calm summer night with a baker's household, from the donkey mills at dusk to the first bread before dawn, told as a slow sleep story.

The bakeries, mills, ovens and loaves are real, found by archaeologists inside the town's walls. Our baker and his family are imagined, drawn from what has been found.

This is a quiet bedtime documentary, narrated slowly to help you relax, unwind, and drift off to sleep. There are no loud sounds, no sudden changes and no horror: just a soft voice, slow images, and the glow of the oven.

About this sleep story

About 59 min, narrated slowly for sleep, with no ad breaks. Made as history to fall asleep to: it's fine to drift off partway, and the chapters below let you find your place again.

Much of what is said online about Roman bread is guesswork. In this episode, what the excavations and ancient writers show is kept separate from what we can only imagine, such as the household itself and the sounds of the night.

Sources

Researched and written for this channel from these sources. Where historians disagree, the narration says so.

  • Mary Beard, Pompeii: The Life of a Roman Town (2008)
  • Alison E. Cooley and M. G. L. Cooley, Pompeii and Herculaneum: A Sourcebook
  • N. Monteix, "Contextualizing the Operational Sequence: Pompeian Bakeries as a Case Study", in Wilson and Flohr (eds), Urban Craftsmen and Traders in the Roman World (OUP, 2016)
  • J. T. Bakker, The Mills-Bakeries of Ostia (1999)
  • J. R. Clarke, Art in the Lives of Ordinary Romans (2003)
  • Pliny the Elder, Natural History 18; Ovid, Fasti 6; Martial, Epigrams 14
  • Parco Archeologico di Ercolano, "Breads and flatbreads"
